title: Canonical vector-bundle base change and direct-sum geometry
statement: Let $S,T$ be Noetherian schemes, let $f:T\to S$, and let $F,G$ be locally free modules of finite constant ranks $r,s$ on their respective bases [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Module inverse image is the tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. For a linear map $a:F\to f_*G$, define the contravariant map $E(G)\to E(F)$ by relative Spec of its unique symmetric-algebra extension [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-core] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec]. It lies over $f$ and pulls the degree-one function of every section $x$ of $F$ to the degree-one function of $a(x)$; these two requirements determine it uniquely. In particular the adjunction unit defines $E(f^*F)\to E(F)$, and its structural square is Cartesian [lem-weil-pbc-relative-spec-base-change]. For two modules $F,G$ on $S$, their biproduct has rank $r+s$. Its total space has the projections induced by the two inclusions, as in [def-pur-vector-purity-direct-sum], and the unique isomorphism $E(p^*F)\cong E(F\oplus G)$ commuting with both projections, where $p:E(G)\to S$. Define the block swap by the biproduct braiding; it is an isomorphism over $S$, so its identity-base square is Cartesian. In rank zero the bundle projection is an isomorphism and its comparison with the identity bundle is Cartesian. The finite-rank bundle projection is affine and of finite type, and its total space is Noetherian, as in the existing integration geometry [def-amb-vector-integration].

proof.text: For any scheme X over S, extend a linear map from F to the direct-image structure module by the symmetric-algebra universal property [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-core]. Compose with the inverse of the existing bundle algebra identification [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. The compatible affine local maps [lem-weil-pbc-affine-algebra-local-maps] glue to a scheme map; equality on affine restrictions proves uniqueness [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Sheaf separation extends the section equation to every open. Underlying algebra morphisms act on module sections by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-space-algebra-module]. Apply this construction to a followed by the generator of E(G) to obtain existsUnique_map; choose its unique witness and use its specification for map_spec.

The preceding mapping property identifies a morphism X to E(F) over the composite X to T to S with a linear map F to f_* rho_* O_X. The tensor-pullback adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] identifies these with maps f^*F to rho_* O_X, hence with maps X to E(f^*F) over T. Evaluating the unit on generators identifies the first projection with the defined baseChange map. Existence and uniqueness of these lifts give a limiting pullback cone. The rank of tensor pullback is transported from the existing usual pullback rank theorem along uniqueness of left adjoints.

Intersect the two Zariski frame covers [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] and restrict the frames. Restriction is additive, so it preserves biproducts. A binary coproduct of the free sheaves on Fin r and Fin s is free on their disjoint union, canonically equivalent to Fin (r+s). These frames prove biprod_rank, including rank zero and an empty cover.

The algebra maps defining purityBundleMap [def-pur-vector-purity-direct-sum] satisfy the generator prescription by the symmetric-algebra universal property. Naturality of the relative-Spec counit [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section] transfers it to scheme maps. Mapping into E(F plus G) is therefore a pair of maps into E(F), E(G) over S, since linear maps out of the biproduct are pairs. This supplies a limiting pullback cone with the existing first and second projections. Uniqueness of pullbacks compares it with the base-change cone from step 2, giving existsUnique_sumIso. Its projection equation and the over-S equation of second give sumIso_isPullback.

Symmetric-algebra extensions of an isomorphism and its inverse compose to identities: check their values on generators and use uniqueness [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-core]. The relative-Spec anti-equivalence carries the biproduct braiding to an isomorphism over S [def-pur-vector-purity-direct-sum, def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Its identity-base square is Cartesian. For rank zero, restrict to the existing frame cover; each bundle chart is affine zero-space, so its projection is invertible. Isomorphisms are Zariski-local at the target, hence zero_isIso and its identity-base pullback square follow.
Reuse the affine, finite-type and Noetherian geometry of the existing integration charts [def-amb-vector-integration-charts]; these are exactly the three registered geometric instances.
